INDEPENDENT AUDIT: NOISY FINITE-CONTROL LINEAR SENSING
2026-10-30. P1 frontier. New audit; earlier reports and control notes unchanged.

VERDICT

The proposed equivalence is correct under the protocol model below. Adaptive
interleaving, readout-dependent directions, randomized encoders, and readout-
dependent stopping do not improve the Bayes risk beyond an optimal static
finite codebook of feasible precision matrices. This is an information result;
the codebook search and coefficient acquisition are not supplied for free by it.

1. MODEL AND PRECISE STATEMENT

Let C be a measurable R^m-valued random vector with E||C||^2 < infinity. Let
V ~ N(0,I_m) be independent of C. The target is F=C^T V. Any normalization of
the target may be included in C. The controller knows C exactly at the outset.
The final estimator has C and the complete legal measurement transcript.

There are at most q measurements, where q is a hard nonnegative integer bound:

    Y_j = a_j^T V + xi_j,     ||a_j||=1,
    xi_1,...,xi_q independent N(0,s),    s>0.

All noise variables, public random seeds, and private random seeds are
independent of (C,V). The actuator chooses a_j using only prior measurement
readouts, received controller bits, and its independent random seed. The
controller can use C, all permitted preceding readouts, and its seed to choose
the next control bits. Feedback may be free, but it contains only functions of
these legal past readouts and independent randomness. The actuator has no
additional access to C or V.

The controller-to-actuator protocol is a binary decision tree with at most B
controller bits on each path. Its timing, termination, measurement requests,
and any other C-dependent actions are charged as control whenever they can
distinguish actuator behavior. Equivalently, after fixing readout randomness
and actuator randomness there are at most N=2^B possible controller branches.
A length cap alone without counting informative timing or unframed stopping
does not establish this property. All policies are measurable and are
totalized on counterfactual histories; every replay has at most q reads.

Define the feasible matrix family

    H_q = { sum_{j=1}^q a_j a_j^T : a_j in R^m, ||a_j||=1 }.

For q=0 this means {0}. One may instead allow up to q rows; the optimal risk is

INDEPENDENT AUDIT: FINITE CONTROL, NOISY GAUSSIAN READS, AND A GENERAL FIRST STAGE
Scientific-computation branch, 2026-10-30.

VERDICT

The proposed exact noisy replay reduction is valid under the access contract
below. The general first-stage decomposition is also valid. The essential
corrections are explicit decoder knowledge, charged control timing, absence
of uncharged correlated actuator side information, and separation of
algorithmic random seeds from the measurement-noise innovations. The replay
freeze includes the innovations only as a mathematical coupling; the posterior
calculation must never reveal those innovations to the predictor.

The intended output is at the controller, or at a decoder retaining the same
first-stage information. The actuator only implements sensing directions and
returns its readouts. This audit does not broaden the theorem to an
actuator-only predictor.

1. CONTRACT THAT MAKES THE THEOREM PRECISE

V~N(0,I_n). C is an R^n-valued random variable independent of V with
E||C||^2<infinity. The controller knows C. The actuator initially has no
C-dependent information except a declared public context Z, if present.
For the unconditional version Z is absent or independent of C.

The actuator can take at most q measurements

  Y_t=u_t^T V+xi_t,  ||u_t||<=1,
  xi_1,...,xi_q iid N(0,s),  s>0.

The innovation sequence is external measurement noise, independent of C,V,
and all algorithmic random seeds. Its realizations are not available to either
party except through the readouts. Directions are predictable from the
actuator's received control bits, previous legal readouts and its algorithmic
seeds. Feedback can return any function of these readouts and seeds, including
the entire readout record, but no extra information about V.

The control protocol has at most B binary controller branches on every path,
so a fixed replay has at most 2^B complete control words. Fixed-length padded
words with a public state deciding when to request the next bit are a
convenient equivalent implementation. Any controller-dependent timing,
stopping, measurement requests, addresses, metadata, or message boundaries
must be included in this control alphabet. A bare payload-length bound with
free termination is insufficient.

or capping at q reads and B bits. This changes no actual
